questions.q: What does an OWD setting of Controlled by Parent mean for an object like Contact?
options: Contacts are always Private regardless of the Account
Contact has no independent OWD — access inherits entirely from the parent Account
Contact access is controlled by the role hierarchy only
Contact requires a separate sharing rule to grant any access
questions.explain: Controlled by Parent means the object has no sharing model of its own — a user's access to a Contact is exactly their access to its parent Account.

questions.q: Why does Contact default to Controlled by Parent instead of an independent OWD level?
options: Because Contact is a custom object
Because a Contact detached from its Account rarely makes sense as an independently-secured thing
Because Salesforce doesn't allow custom OWD settings on standard objects
Because Contact records can't be shared
questions.explain: Objects like Contact and Asset are conceptually part of their parent record, so maintaining a separate sharing model for them would be pointless duplication.

questions.q: What does Grant Access Using Hierarchies control?
options: Whether field-level security applies to an object
Whether the role hierarchy is allowed to apply to that object's or group's sharing
Whether a public group can contain other public groups
Whether manual sharing is enabled org-wide
questions.explain: This checkbox determines whether the role hierarchy's automatic upward visibility applies — turning it off makes seniority not translate into automatic record access.

questions.q: Where does Grant Access Using Hierarchies appear?
options: Only on the OWD page
Only when creating a new public group
On OWD rows and on a public group's own detail/creation page
Only in Field-Level Security settings
questions.explain: It's a property that appears both at the OWD level and on sharing recipients like public groups — it's not a one-time, single-location toggle.

questions.q: Why is turning off Grant Access Using Hierarchies rare?
options: It's disabled by Salesforce for all orgs
It can make a manager genuinely unable to see records through the hierarchy alone, which most orgs don't want
It requires a special license
It only works on custom objects with Master-Detail relationships
questions.explain: Turning it off deliberately breaks the usual assumption that management structure grants visibility — unusual enough that most orgs never touch it.
